entities.summary:
Gil de Siloé was a Flemish sculptor born in Antwerp in 1500 and died in 1501, whose late Gothic works in Burgos showcased a unique style that blended Isabelline and Burgundian influences.





Gil de Siloé was influenced by the artistic innovations of the Burgundian court, where he trained under the renowned sculptor Claus Sluter.






The sculptor's work in Burgos, including his famous tomb in the Burgos Cathedral, contributed to the city's growth as a major artistic center during the late Middle Ages.




Gil de Siloé's style, characterized by its blend of Gothic and Renaissance elements, was later adopted by other sculptors in the Iberian Peninsula and beyond.


Gil de Siloé's legacy can be seen in the many surviving examples of his work, including the tomb of Rodrigo Ponce de León in the Cathedral of Santo Domingo in Burgos, which remains one of the finest examples of late Gothic sculpture in Spain.


In a surprising twist, the sculptor's relatively short career was marked by a significant artistic output, with many of his works now considered masterpieces of the late Gothic period.
